name: Cold waves & winter storms
summary: No top-tier cold or winter-storm warning across a major region on 16 Nov; heavy snow confined to western mountains
state: The storm that crossed the eastern US from 12 Nov brought the season's first widespread snow to New England and the Appalachians, with ski areas expecting 3 to 6 inches, and two storms were forecast to bring 1 to 2 feet to the Sierra Nevada and Oregon Cascades by 16 Nov (OpenSnow, 11 Nov). Warmer, drier conditions were forecast for eastern North America from 16 to 20 Nov. Searches on 16 Nov found no top-tier warning across a major region and no cold-related power or gas outages, so Normal is kept.
for_you: Mountain travel in the western US can be disrupted by heavy snow. People in affected areas should follow National Weather Service warnings; in the UK, follow Met Office warnings as winter approaches.
rubric_hit: No major cold wave or winter storm affecting large populations: Normal

sources.title: OpenSnow — US and Canada Daily Snow

why: Severe cold and winter storms kill, cut power and spike gas demand, as in Texas in 2021; they matter most when energy supplies are tight.
drivers: Polar vortex disruption, blocking highs, ENSO, Arctic outbreaks.

rubric.alert: Deadly cold or winter storms with widespread power or gas outages.
rubric.watch: Top-tier cold or winter-storm warnings across a major region, or a cold wave lifting gas demand sharply.
rubric.normal: No major cold wave or winter storm affecting large populations.
